Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National | Top Story Court dismisses Wontumi’s bail application pending appeal Source : Myjoyonline 16 November 2026 10:05am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
An Accra High Court has dismissed an application by former New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, seeking bail pending an appeal against his 20-year prison sentence.
The court held that Mr Boasiako had failed to demonstrate that his appeal raised arguable grounds with a reasonable prospect of success to justify his release while the appeal process continued.
The decision means Mr Boasiako will remain in prison as he pursues his appeal against his conviction and sentence.
His lawyers, led by Samuel Atta Akyea, had urged the court to grant him temporary freedom, arguing that the conviction was affected by serious errors of law and that the appeal had strong prospects of success.
They relied on 19 grounds of appeal, including arguments that the trial judge misinterpreted provisions of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), and wrongly attributed criminal liability to their client despite the separate legal personality of Akonta Mining Company Limited.
The defence also argued that Mr Boasiako was not a flight risk, pointing out that he had complied with his bail conditions throughout the trial and that his passport remained in the custody of the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO).
However, the State, represented by Deputy Attorney-General Dr Justice Srem-Sai, opposed the application, insisting that the former NPP regional chairman had not established exceptional circumstances to warrant bail.
The prosecution maintained that the appeal had no reasonable prospect of success and argued that Mr Boasiako posed a flight risk, particularly because he was facing two other criminal cases that could result in additional prison sentences.
Mr Boasiako was on July 20, 2026, sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment with hard labour by the High Court, presided over by Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay, after being convicted of mining-related offences involving Akonta Mining Company's concession at Samreboi in the Western Region.
He was found guilty of assigning mineral rights without the required ministerial approval and intentionally facilitating an unlicensed mining operation, contrary to the Minerals and Mining Act.
The court also imposed financial penalties on him and Akonta Mining Company Limited.
Dissatisfied with the conviction and sentence, Mr Boasiako subsequently filed an appeal challenging the trial court's decision and applied for bail pending its determination.
His bail application was initially scheduled for August 19 but was adjourned to October 15 after the trial judge was unable to sit due to ill health.
After hearing arguments from both sides on October 15, the court fixed November 4 to deliver its ruling. The ruling was subsequently delayed amid disruptions to court proceedings following the nationwide strike by members of the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG).
The dismissal of the bail application does not determine the substantive appeal against his conviction and 20-year prison sentence.
